_comment: The libgit2 port campaign's order of modules and its waves, schema 6, as planner run 4 planned them
over the whole target, the libgit2.so link unit and the git2 CLI executable, run 5 corrected them and
run 6 converted them to schema 6 with the later stages of a port campaign. modules and the todo waves
come from one wavefront schedule of crustify/wavefront/configs/wavefront-config.json in its default,
body-deep mode, every module's files seeded, enums scheduled (--with-enums), no batch caps; modules
are listed by layer. One departure from wavefront's order: each foundational module's uses of other
modules (src/util/errors.c's git_error_set_oom and git_error_set on alloc.c's, strlist.c's and
win32_leakcheck.c's failure paths) are cut, so the foundational modules come first, and every layer
is the longest path over the scheduled dependencies that remain. Waves 0-168 are the wrap campaign's
that had started (88 done, 1 wip): kept as they ran, their items those of their batches, each with
its batch's kind as objective; the 17 wip waves of port modules were closed with the batches that
had landed, at the user's request. The todo waves have no batches. Each item's objective follows its
module's: in the seven foundational modules, which are wrap in every campaign, the items other
modules can reach (exported and header-inline functions, extern globals, callbacks, and the types a
header declares) are wrap, their statics and enums planned for none; in every other module, which
the port campaign ports, every function, global, callback, enum and type generator is port where the
order places it, and a struct or union is port there when no layout user of another module remains
(its opaque_after names no other module), wrap otherwise. The later stages follow each item's release
points, which every planned item carries as wavefront 2a95e3c records them, their waves renumbered to
this schedule's and their modules written {link_unit, module, foundational}: port/layout after a
type's opaque_after, port/memory after its memory_unmanaged_after, port/unexport after a ported
function's or global's unreferenced_after, each when the point names a module other than the item's
own, and none when a user stays C in a foundational module. The C tests count as referrers too,
though wavefront's closure leaves them out: a test file tied to modules (modules.json tests) leaves
with the first of them to be integrated, so a stage the test still calls also waits for one of them,
and a test tied to no port module keeps the export for good. The stages the same integrations free
share a wave of the item's module, after its translation waves, which depends on the last
translation wave of each freeing module, the run that integrates its C. An item a started wave's
batches hold, or that a batch landed, with that objective is not planned again, and a dependency on
it is one on that wave. A translation wave's depends_on is recomputed from its items' unit edges:
scheduled, its module's previous wave and the earlier waves holding their dependencies; cut, the
later ones. Out of scope: the deprecated git_url_resolve_cb and the GIT_DEPRECATE_HARD-only field
users (commit_id, signing_cb, resolve_url, update_tips). A module's external records count its units'
references to out-of-tree entities, macros and compiler builtins left out, by the library whose
installed headers define them. Homes follow the conventions: src/<link-unit>/<TU path>.rs, a header
module's <stem>_h.rs. Planner run 6's composition is crustify/artifacts/planner/run-6/compose/.
